# ModelComp — AI Model Comparison Platform

## Project Introduction

**ModelComp** is a static website that provides comprehensive side-by-side comparisons of AI coding models. The platform focuses on what truly matters for developers: tool use capabilities, reasoning abilities, context window size, multimodal support, coding proficiency, and cost efficiency. Each model receives normalized scores from 1-100 across these dimensions, with an Overall score calculated per model plus per-reporter grades showing how different evaluation agents rate each other.

### Core Goals and Objectives

- **Data-Driven Comparisons**: Every score displayed on the site is parsed at build time from research files, eliminating hardcoded numbers in the UI
- **Multi-Agent Evaluation**: Models are evaluated by various reporting agents (Claude, Gemini, GPT, etc.) to provide diverse perspectives
- **Transparent Methodology**: Clear scoring methodology with six key dimensions and independent cost efficiency scoring
- **Developer-Focused**: Emphasis on practical coding benchmarks and real-world performance metrics

### Target Audience

- Software developers evaluating AI models for coding tasks
- Technical teams comparing model capabilities and costs
- Researchers studying AI model performance trends
- Open-source contributors interested in AI model benchmarking

## Technical Architecture

The project follows a modern static site generation architecture built on Qwik framework with a data-driven approach:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Research Files] --> B[Sync Script]
    B --> C[Generated Data]
    C --> D[Qwik Components]
    D --> E[Static Site]
    
    F[Model Folders] --> B
    G[Meta JSON] --> B
    
    H[Compare Section] --> I[HexRadar Chart]
    H --> J[Model Cards]
    H --> K[Score Tables]
    
    L[Model Pages] --> M[Per-Model Details]
    L --> N[Agent Grades Table]
```

### Component Breakdown

The application is structured around several key architectural patterns:

**Data Pipeline Architecture**: Research markdown files → Sync script → Generated TypeScript → Runtime components

**Component Composition Pattern**: Reusable UI components (HexRadar, ModelCards, ModelSelect) composed into larger sections

**Configuration-Driven Design**: Model metadata and scoring rules defined in JSON/Markdown rather than code

**Static Site Generation**: All pages pre-rendered at build time for optimal performance

### System Relationships

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[model/<slug>/] --> B[sync-data.mjs]
    B --> C[scores.generated.ts]
    B --> D[sources.generated.ts]
    C --> E[src/data/models.ts]
    D --> E
    E --> F[UI Components]
    
    G[meta.json] --> E
    H[findings.md] --> B
```

## Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points

- **Application Root**: `src/root.tsx` - Qwik application bootstrap with theme handling and PWA setup
- **Data Layer**: `src/data/models.ts` - Central model hydration and scoring logic
- **Build Scripts**: `scripts/sync-data.mjs` - Deterministic data synchronization pipeline

### Core Modules

**Data Management System**:
- `src/data/models.ts` - Model hydration, scoring calculations, and source registry management
- `src/data/scores.generated.ts` - Pre-parsed model scores (auto-generated)
- `src/data/sources.generated.ts` - Reporting agent registry (auto-generated)

**UI Components**:
- `src/components/CompareSection.tsx` - Main comparison interface with hexagonal radar charts
- `src/components/HexRadar.tsx` - Interactive radar chart visualization
- `src/components/ModelCards.tsx` - Model display cards with detailed information
- `src/components/ModelSelect.tsx` - Model selection dropdowns

### Configuration Approach

**Build Configuration**:
- `vite.config.ts` - Vite build configuration for Qwik framework
- `tailwind.config.js` - Tailwind CSS customization
- `postcss.config.js` - PostCSS processing pipeline

**Runtime Configuration**:
- Theme system using CSS variables and dark mode support
- PWA manifest for mobile app installation
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach

### External Dependencies

**Core Framework Stack**:
- Qwik 1.20 + Qwik City for resumable web applications
- Vite 7 for fast build tooling
- TypeScript 5.6 for type safety
- Tailwind CSS v3.4 for utility-first styling

**Development Tools**:
- pnpm 9.15.4 for package management
- Node.js ≥ 18.17 runtime requirements

### Integration Points

**Data Source Integration**:
- Markdown-based research files for model evaluations
- JSON metadata for model information
- Automated sync pipeline for data consistency

**Deployment Integration**:
- Static site generation for CDN deployment
- PWA support for offline functionality
- SEO optimization through SSR

### Component Relationship Diagrams

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class CompareSection {
        +a: string
        +b: string
        +c: string
        +source: ResultsView
        +onSelect$()
        +onSource$()
    }
    
    class HexRadar {
        +series: RadarDatum[]
        +renderChart()
    }
    
    class ModelCards {
        +models: AiModel[]
        +renderCards()
    }
    
    class ModelSelect {
        +value: string
        +options: Option[]
        +onChange$()
    }
    
    CompareSection --> HexRadar
    CompareSection --> ModelSelect
```

### Functionality Overview

**Model Comparison Interface**:
- Side-by-side comparison of up to three models simultaneously
- Interactive hexagonal radar chart showing six performance dimensions
- Detailed score tables with sorting and filtering capabilities
- Real-time switching between different result sources

**Per-Model Detail Pages**:
- Individual model pages with comprehensive information
- Agent-specific grading breakdowns
- Context window and modality specifications
- Pricing information and cost efficiency analysis

**Dynamic Data Processing**:
- Automated score calculation and validation
- Multi-agent averaging with quality gates
- Real-time source registration and model discovery

### Implementation Highlights

**Advanced Scoring System**:
- Six-dimensional scoring: Tool use, Reasoning, Context window, Multimodal, Coding, Cost efficiency
- Independent cost efficiency scoring separate from overall quality metrics
- Quality-gated averaging excluding low-quality raters (Overall < 84.9)

**Interactive Visualizations**:
- Custom hexagonal radar chart implementation
- Responsive design adapting to mobile and desktop screens
- Dark/light theme support with smooth transitions

**Robust Data Pipeline**:
- Deterministic sync process ensuring data consistency
- Comprehensive validation and error handling
- Automatic quarantine of invalid or excluded reports
